questions.problem:
Let $R=[0,2]\times [1,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=13-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{0,1,2\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,2,3\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the lower Riemann sum $L(f,P).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/4faf932e63a57d2fe53fb3942cfe21c65d0d2a88692c665b2706bd68164855c9.png)

The lower Riemann sum $L(f,P)$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{m}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{m}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{m}_{22}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22})
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the minimum value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *minimum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *lower* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=1$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $L(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}+{m}_{21}+{m}_{12}+{m}_{22}.
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=13-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=13-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/e70e2cf07b27a91c34e59435229302f3b2127b15a2f39049c0a8389cd6f59863.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/aa3858dba149ebf5650ed06f75444244494fe0a961f897100914d54f6d7c0b49.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{11} & =f(1,2)=8 \\ {m}_{21} & =f(2,2)=5 \\ {m}_{12} & =f(1,3)=3 \\ {m}_{22} & =f(2,3)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
L(f,P)=8+5+3+0=16.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/5d5af7cb2f2b12a52bb624d12938aafd2d34b079ad5d28dc44133292b98956ec.png)

Consider the partition of the rectangular region $R$ shown above and the positive function $f(x,y)$ defined on $R.$ Which of the following gives an expression for the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to this partition.

*Hint: ${m}_{ij}$ denotes the minimum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}$*
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the lower Riemann sum $L$ with respect to the given partition, we compute the sum of the volumes of $3$ rectangular solids, one for each ${R}_{ij}.$

The volume of the rectangular solid corresponding to each subregion ${R}_{ij}$ is given by

$$
{m}_{ij}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{ij}).
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ denotes the minimum value of $f$ on the subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *minimum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *lower* sum.

So in our case, we have

$$
L={m}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{m}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{m}_{31}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{31}).
$$

Notice that

$$
\text{Area}({R}_{11})=\text{Area}({R}_{21})=\text{Area}({R}_{31})=2.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =2\cdot {m}_{11}+2\cdot {m}_{21}+2\cdot {m}_{31} \\  & =2({m}_{11}+{m}_{21}+{m}_{31}).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $R=[1,3]\times [1,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=13-2x-2y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}=\{1,2,3\},\,{P}_{2}=\{1,2,3\},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the lower Riemann sum $L(f,P).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/46b590842cb6dd1cb994318be3a35ef0f7782542d3a74c4f788180577ab50301.png)

The lower Riemann sum $L(f,P)$ is given by

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{m}_{21}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{21})+{m}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{m}_{22}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{22})
$$

where ${m}_{ij}$ is the minimum value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *minimum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *lower* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=1$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $L(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
L(f,P)={m}_{11}+{m}_{21}+{m}_{12}+{m}_{22}.
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=13-2x-2y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=13-2x-2y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/52c19da39a43cdbf1b1d2565669c391e59679b3bf9828f7c46755831b2b0890c.png)

As a result, the *minimum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *largest* possible $x$ and the *largest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *top right corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14270560/assets/2acddf617eda8211e45d281329051f08a8b83788e24b70ebe8d526b58b195bba.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{11} & =f(2,2)=5 \\ {m}_{21} & =f(3,2)=3 \\ {m}_{12} & =f(2,3)=3 \\ {m}_{22} & =f(3,3)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
L(f,P)=5+3+3+1=12.
$$
